name: Danielle Prosser
presenting_complaint: Sudden worst-ever headache, maximal at onset

medical_history.social: Smoker 10/day. Occasional alcohol. Works as a schoolteacher.
medical_history.family: Mother had a 'brain bleed' in her 50s. Polycystic kidney disease in an aunt.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 47-year-old woman presents with a sudden, severe headache that reached maximum intensity within seconds (thunderclap) while gardening 2 hours ago. She describes it as the worst headache of her life, with neck stiffness and one episode of vomiting. She is alert (GCS 15) but distressed. BP 168/96. This is a suspected subarachnoid haemorrhage.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Headache characterised as thunderclap: maximal at onset (peak within seconds to minutes), worst-ever
Red-flag screen: exertional/coital onset, neck stiffness, drowsiness, focal signs, seizure, photophobia, age over 50, immunosuppressed, anticoagulated, fever
Associated symptoms: vomiting, visual change, sentinel headache in preceding weeks
Risk factors: family history of SAH/aneurysm, polycystic kidney disease, smoking, hypertension
State explicitly: a normal CT after 6 hours does NOT exclude SAH
objective: Urgent non-contrast CT brain — most sensitive within 6 hours of onset (FIRST investigation)
Full neurological exam: GCS, pupils, focal deficit, meningism/neck stiffness
Obs and cardiac monitor; document time of headache onset precisely
If CT negative and story convincing: lumbar puncture at 12 hours from onset for xanthochromia (or CTA per senior decision)
assessment: Subarachnoid haemorrhage until proven otherwise given thunderclap headache
Differentials: migraine, meningitis, cervical artery dissection, venous sinus thrombosis, reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
Recognise that a normal CT beyond 6 hours does not exclude SAH
plan: Urgent non-contrast CT brain immediately (FIRST action)
A-to-E, IV access, analgesia (e.g. paracetamol/opioid), antiemetic, cardiac monitor
Control extreme hypertension only on senior advice (avoid over-aggressive lowering)
If CT negative but story convincing: LP at 12 hours from onset for xanthochromia, or CTA — senior/neurosurgical decision
Bloods: FBC, UEC, coags, group and hold; reverse any anticoagulation
Nimodipine 60 mg orally every 4 hours once SAH confirmed (per neurosurgery) to reduce vasospasm
Call ED consultant and neurosurgery; keep nil by mouth pending decisions

critical_errors: Assuming a normal CT rules out SAH — outside the 6-hour window a normal CT does NOT exclude it, so failing to proceed to LP for xanthochromia (or CTA) when the story is convincing is an automatic fail
Discharging a thunderclap-headache patient without excluding SAH
must_not_miss: Subarachnoid haemorrhage considered and actively excluded (CT +/- LP for xanthochromia)
Bacterial meningitis considered in the differential
Precise documentation of time of headache onset to interpret CT sensitivity
